name: Matcha
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: dry powder as sold, reported on the as-sold article; matcha is whisked into water and ingested in its entirety, so the as-sold powder basis is also the basis in which the consumer's whole dose is delivered
scope_note: Stone-ground Camellia sinensis leaf powder (matcha, and culinary-grade matcha sold for beverage preparation), including matcha-based latte and drink powders whose matcha content is the dominant characterising ingredient. Split out from the true-tea row for one mechanistic reason that changes the exposure arithmetic rather than the number: matcha is suspended and swallowed whole, so the entire contaminant load of the leaf is ingested, whereas an infused leaf transfers only the extractable fraction and is discarded. The published ceiling is the same government value that binds tea leaf, because that is the only sovereign value for the commodity; the difference is that in this row it is a whole-dose ceiling, which is disclosed on the aluminium and lead cells. A matcha product with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16; a sweetened matcha drink mix whose dominant ingredient is sugar or dairy solids routes to the cocoa-and-malted-beverage-mix row's basis treatment by analogy and is certified there.
basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.label: Matcha is green tea, so Hong Kong Cap 132V's Tea, Green, Black lead cell (5000 ug/kg, as sold) is a DIRECT sovereign maximum level for this product form and basis, not a read-across. It is the only credible sovereign lead value for the commodity and it binds.
Pb.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup: matcha is Camellia sinensis leaf, ground rather than left whole, and no credible instrument writes a separate cell for the ground form, so the commodity cell applies as written. The consequence is disclosed rather than smoothed: because matcha is ingested whole, a lot at the 5000 ug/kg ceiling delivers the full leaf lead burden to the consumer, where an infusion made from leaf at the same ceiling would deliver only the extractable fraction and Hong Kong's own beverage cell would cap the resulting drink at 200 ug/kg. HMTc does not resolve that asymmetry by inventing an extraction-corrected number, which Method v2.0 forbids; it publishes the government value, flags the whole-leaf ingestion route on the certificate, and treats this cell as a first-order Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12, where certified-lot evidence is the only admissible basis for a lower value.

Cd.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for matcha powder. No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for tea in any form. As with lead, the whole-leaf ingestion route makes this a live cell rather than a formality, and the absence of a sovereign ceiling is disclosed rather than filled. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
Cd.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

tAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for matcha powder. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. No sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic cell for tea in any form, so both arsenic cells in this row are controls and the escalation rule carries the obligation. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
tAs.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for matcha powder. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell is scoped either to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to packaged and public drinking water. None of those is applicable to this dry commodity, and applying a ready-to-drink beverage cell to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation. Inorganic arsenic is a Tier-1 analyte, so it is speciated whenever the total-arsenic screen is elevated.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot exceeds 100 ug/kg in the as-sold dry basis; a confirmed inorganic-arsenic result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.

tHg.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for matcha powder. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
tHg.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in dry matcha powder: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for matcha powder. EU 2024/1987 is the only comprehensive sovereign nickel instrument; its cells cover cereals, pulses, oilseeds, tree nuts, vegetables, cocoa and chocolate, infant formula, baby food and fruit and vegetable juices, and none of them covers this commodity. The juice and nectar cell (250 ug/kg) is written in a ready-to-drink basis and cannot be applied to a dry commodity, and the dry-commodity cells that do exist are written for other plant families. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte on the mandatory eight-total panel.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. An elevated result escalates to a soil, cultivar and stainless-equipment investigation.

Sn.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a tin maximum level for dry matcha powder. The exclusion is written into the instrument itself: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5 scopes its inorganic-tin maximum levels to canned beverages and canned foods and expressly excepts canned dried and canned powdered products, and the Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong canned-food cells carry the same carve-out. There is therefore no sovereign number for a dry beverage commodity and no supportable read-across, because the canned-liquid cells are written in a ready-to-drink basis. Tin is nonetheless on the mandatory eight-total panel.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. Where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink form of this product, that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin maximum level in the as-consumed basis.

companions.scope: canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, except ca

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for matcha powder, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable: the only sovereign aluminium values are packaged-drinking-water quality standards written in a litre-of-water basis (Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1). Applying a water-basis value to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation of roughly three orders of magnitude. Aluminium is the highest-priority control in this row. Camellia sinensis is an aluminium hyperaccumulator, and matcha delivers the whole leaf rather than an infusion, so the aluminium the leaf accumulated is ingested in full rather than partially extracted. No credible sovereign has written a ceiling for tea in any form. HMTc mandates aluminium on every certified lot, reports it on the certificate with the whole-leaf ingestion route stated, and declines to invent a number; the analyte is a first-order Standards Ratchet surveillance priority.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for matcha powder. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: this row's certified article is a DRY powder, so there is no aqueous matrix in which Cr(VI) could be reduced to Cr(III), and the acidic-beverage reduction argument is unavailable. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
